# Retro Diffusion API — context for AI agents (verified 2026-09)
Pixel art image generation API. Default base URL for new integrations: https://api.retrodiffusion.ai/v2
V1 remains supported with no retirement plan at https://api.retrodiffusion.ai/v1. V2 uses {"error":{"code":"...","message":"...","request_id":"..."}} for every JSON error. Preserve X-Request-ID and Retry-After, branch on code, and never retry a paid failure across versions.
Full human-readable reference (with an interactive style explorer): https://www.retrodiffusion.ai/app/guide/api
Runnable example scripts: https://github.com/Retro-Diffusion/api-examples/tree/main/example-scripts
Auth: send header "X-RD-Token: <key>" on every request. Keys start with "rdpk-".
Humans create keys at https://www.retrodiffusion.ai/app/devtools (max 5 per account).
Prefer MCP if available: https://mcp.retrodiffusion.ai/mcp (HTTP transport, header "Authorization: Bearer <key>").
MCP tools (29): create_inference, estimate_inference_cost (free), start_inference_job + get_inference_job (async jobs — recommended for animations and batches; success results carry hosted output_urls, not base64), list_inference_jobs, get_inference_result, list_available_styles, list_available_models, get_style_usage, list_edit_tools, run_edit_tool, estimate_edit_tool_cost (free), fix_pixel_art (free), create_user_style, update_user_style, delete_user_style, Low-Poly 3D: get_lowpoly_pricing, estimate_lowpoly_cost (free), start_lowpoly_generate, start_lowpoly_revise, start_lowpoly_animate (pass animation to change an existing one), get_lowpoly_job, get_lowpoly_model, list_lowpoly_models, export_lowpoly_model; authenticate, get_balance, get_service_status, logout. Tip: pass upload_outputs=true on create_inference to receive hosted URLs instead of base64 payloads.
MCP setup guides for every client (Claude Code + plugin, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Claude Desktop) live at https://github.com/Retro-Diffusion/retro-diffusion-mcp.

## Generate images
POST /v2/inferences  (Content-Type: application/json)
Required fields: width (int), height (int), num_images (int). Send prompt_style to select a style. prompt defaults to an empty string and is required only when the selected style's prompt_requirement says so; image-driven styles may accept an empty prompt.
Optional fields: seed (int, reproducible), input_image (base64 PNG string, NO "data:image/png;base64," prefix, RGB without transparency) + strength (float 0-1, default 0.75 — how much to change the input), reference_images (array of base64, RD Pro styles only, up to 9, guides style/content without redrawing), input_palette (base64, constrains output colors), remove_bg (bool, transparent output), tile_x / tile_y (bool, seamless tiling), frames_duration (int 4|6|8|10|12|16, animation styles; ignored by rd_advanced_animation__rotate), return_spritesheet (bool, animations: PNG spritesheet instead of GIF; for rd_advanced_animation__rotate the 3x3 direction sheet), upscale_output_factor (int, 1 = native pixel size), bypass_prompt_expansion (bool, skip automatic LLM prompt enrichment), include_downloadable_data (bool, extra structured assets e.g. item atlas JSON), check_cost (bool, FREE dry run: returns price, generates nothing, charges nothing), async (bool, accepted for source compatibility; v2 generation is always async).
The "negative" field exists but is a placeholder — current models ignore it. Do not rely on it.
Size limits: the API validates 12x12 to 512x512, but each style enforces tighter limits (current styles top out at 384x384; several RD Pro styles go down to 12x12) — use the per-style limits in the catalog below or from the selector.
Before a paid submission, persist a unique Idempotency-Key (1-256 visible ASCII characters). Reuse that key only with identical inputs when the admission response is uncertain. Once task_id is known, poll that task instead of submitting again. Do not send Idempotency-Key on check_cost requests or edit/pixel-fixer routes.

### Example: minimal request
POST /v2/inferences
Headers: X-RD-Token: <key>, Idempotency-Key: <persisted-generation-key>
{"prompt": "A knight resting by a campfire in a forest clearing at night", "prompt_style": "rd_fast__default", "width": 128, "height": 128, "num_images": 1, "seed": 77}
### Example: accepted response
{"status": "accepted", "task_id": "8d24e990-...", "request_id": "8d24e990-...", "message": "Inference accepted. Poll GET /v2/inferences/tasks/{task_id} for status."}
Poll the task. When it succeeds, `result` contains the generation response:
{"created_at": 1783523045, "balance_cost": 0.019, "base64_images": ["iVBORw0KGgo..."], "model": "rd_fast", "remaining_balance": 100.75, "request_id": "8d24e990-...", "outputs_retained_until": 1783609445}
base64_images entries are raw base64 PNG (or GIF for animation styles). Decode and write to disk. Add "upload_outputs": true to receive hosted URLs in "output_urls" instead. Large results (notably multi-frame animations) are delivered as hosted output_urls automatically with base64_images empty — always handle both fields, exactly like the edit tools.

### Example: img2img
{"prompt": "The same scene in deep winter, snow covered", "prompt_style": "rd_plus__default", "width": 128, "height": 128, "num_images": 1, "input_image": "<base64>", "strength": 0.8}
### Example: RD Pro with reference images (character/style consistency)
{"prompt": "The same goblin merchant, now sitting by a campfire counting gold coins", "prompt_style": "rd_pro__default", "width": 128, "height": 128, "num_images": 1, "reference_images": ["<base64 of the original character>"]}
### Example: advanced animation (animate an uploaded start frame; input_image REQUIRED; output is a GIF)
{"prompt": "Confident, steady steps", "prompt_style": "rd_advanced_animation__walking", "width": 64, "height": 64, "num_images": 1, "frames_duration": 8, "input_image": "<base64 start frame, match width/height>"}
### Example: 8 directional views of an uploaded sprite (input_image REQUIRED; prompt is an OPTIONAL subject hint; no frames_duration)
{"prompt": "", "prompt_style": "rd_advanced_animation__rotate", "width": 64, "height": 64, "num_images": 1, "input_image": "<base64 sprite, 32-256px, multiples of 8>", "remove_bg": true, "return_spritesheet": true}
### Example: advanced tileset (two textures)
{"prompt": "grey stones with gravel", "extra_prompt": "lush green grass", "prompt_style": "rd_tile__tileset_advanced", "width": 16, "height": 16, "num_images": 1}
### Example: free cost check (never charges)
{"prompt": "test", "prompt_style": "rd_pro__default", "width": 256, "height": 256, "num_images": 2, "check_cost": true}
-> {"balance_cost": 0.36, "model": "check_cost", "base64_images": [], "remaining_balance": 100.75}

## Async jobs (required for every v2 generation)
POST /v2/inferences (the optional "async": true field is retained for source compatibility)
-> {"status": "accepted", "task_id": "8d24e990-...", "request_id": "8d24e990-...", "message": "Inference accepted. Poll GET /v2/inferences/tasks/{task_id} for status."}
Poll GET /v2/inferences/tasks/{task_id} (same X-RD-Token) every ~2s:
-> {"status": "pending" | "running" | "succeeded" | "failed", "task_id": "...", "result": <same shape as sync response, when succeeded>, "error": {"status_code": 400, "detail": "..."} when failed}
After a lost submission response, retry identical inputs with the persisted Idempotency-Key. If the key is unavailable, list recent jobs and resume polling instead of blindly resubmitting:
GET /v2/inferences/tasks?limit=20 (optional &status=pending|running|succeeded|failed), newest first:
-> {"tasks": [{"task_id": "...", "status": "running", "created_at": ..., "updated_at": ..., "result": null, "error": null}, ...]}

## Style catalog (public styles)
RD Pro (highest quality, supports reference_images, $0.18/image): rd_pro__default, rd_pro__painterly, rd_pro__fantasy, rd_pro__horror, rd_pro__scifi, rd_pro__simple, rd_pro__isometric, rd_pro__topdown, rd_pro__platformer — all (12-256px, batch<=16, refs<=9); rd_pro__dungeon_map, rd_pro__spritesheet, rd_pro__fps_weapon, rd_pro__typography (64-256px, batch<=4, refs<=9); rd_pro__hexagonal_tiles, rd_pro__ui_panel, rd_pro__inventory_items (256x256 only, batch<=4, refs<=9); rd_pro__pixelate (16-256px, batch<=16, refs<=9, INPUT_IMAGE_REQUIRED); rd_pro__edit (64-256px, batch<=4, refs<=9, INPUT_IMAGE_REQUIRED).
RD Plus (quality all-rounder): rd_plus__default, rd_plus__retro, rd_plus__watercolor, rd_plus__textured, rd_plus__cartoon, rd_plus__ui_element, rd_plus__item_sheet, rd_plus__character_turnaround, rd_plus__environment, rd_plus__isometric, rd_plus__isometric_asset, rd_plus__topdown_map, rd_plus__topdown_asset — all (64-384px, batch<=16); rd_plus__classic, rd_plus__skill_icon (32-192px); rd_plus__low_res, rd_plus__mc_item, rd_plus__mc_texture (16-128px); rd_plus__topdown_item (16-96px).
RD Fast (fastest/cheapest): rd_fast__default (batch<=15), rd_fast__simple, rd_fast__detailed, rd_fast__retro, rd_fast__game_asset, rd_fast__portrait, rd_fast__texture, rd_fast__ui, rd_fast__item_sheet, rd_fast__character_turnaround, rd_fast__no_style, rd_fast__1_bit — all (64-384px, batch<=16); rd_fast__low_res, rd_fast__mc_item, rd_fast__mc_texture (16-128px). (The selector may return internal ids like "default:rd_flux" for these — both forms are accepted.)
RD Mini (aliases routing to Plus/Fast low-res; response "model" shows the routed model): rd_mini__classic, rd_mini__skill_icon (32-192px); rd_mini__low_res, rd_mini__mc_item, rd_mini__mc_texture, rd_mini__fast_low_res, rd_mini__fast_mc_item, rd_mini__fast_mc_texture (16-128px); rd_mini__topdown_item (16-96px) — all batch<=16.
Advanced animations (INPUT_IMAGE_REQUIRED, 32-256px matching your start frame, batch=1, frames_duration supported, GIF output): rd_advanced_animation__walking, __idle, __jump, __crouch, __attack, __destroy, __custom_action (describe any motion), __subtle_motion (ambient scene motion), __rotate (the other 7 directional views of the uploaded subject, not motion: prompt OPTIONAL subject hint, size a multiple of 8, remove_bg/input_palette supported, frames_duration ignored; GIF of 8 views by default, return_spritesheet=true gives a 3x3 PNG sheet with an empty center where every view faces the center: top=front, bottom=back, left/right=sides, corners=diagonals — same layout and frame order as rd_animation__8_dir_rotation; cost 0.10).
Animations (prompt-driven, GIF output, batch=1 unless noted): rd_animation__four_angle_walking (48x48), rd_animation__four_angle_walking_idle (48x48), rd_animation__small_sprites (32x32, batch<=16), rd_animation__vfx (24-96px square), rd_animation__any_animation (64x64, refs<=9), rd_animation__big_animation (128x128, refs<=9), rd_animation__8_dir_rotation (80x80, refs<=5), rd_animation__battle_sprites (64x64).
Tilesets: rd_tile__tileset (16-32px tile, batch=1), rd_tile__tileset_advanced (16-32px, batch=1, extra_prompt + extra_input_image), rd_tile__single_tile (16-64px), rd_tile__tile_variation (16-128px, INPUT_IMAGE_REQUIRED), rd_tile__tile_object (16-96px), rd_tile__scene_object (64-384px).
User styles: user__<name>_<id> (created via /v2/styles or the My Styles page).
Live discovery: GET /v2/styles/selector (optional ?model=rd_fast|rd_plus|rd_pro|rd_mini, ?tab=tab:image|tab:animation|tab:advanced-animation|tab:tileset). Each item: {"prompt_style", "name", "description", "required_model", "required_tab", "min_width", "max_width", "min_height", "max_height", "max_number_of_images", "require_input_image", "prompt_requirement", "supports_frames_duration", "supports_reference_images", "example_prompt"}.

## Costs (USD per request; verify with check_cost — it is free)
rd_fast: max(0.015, (w*h+100000)/6000000) * num_images; rd_plus: max(0.025, (w*h+50000)/2000000) * num_images; low-res styles (mc_*, low_res, classic, skill_icon, topdown_item, tile variants): max(0.02, (w*h+13700)/600000) * num_images; rd_pro: 0.18 * num_images; rd_advanced_animation: 0.14 (custom_action and subtle_motion: 0.25; rotate: 0.10); rd_animation: 0.07 (any_animation and 8_dir_rotation: 0.25); rd_tile__tileset(_advanced): 0.10.
GET /v2/inferences/credits -> {"credits": 0, "balance": 100.75}. Balance is prepaid USD; charged before generation, auto-refunded on failure. Invalid token on this endpoint -> 401 invalid_token.

## Canvas edit tools (post-processing; canonical fields use snake_case)
GET /v2/edit/tools -> enabled tool list with api_fields, costs, defaults, and limits (authoritative; exposed tools may vary).
POST /v2/edit/tools/{tool_id} -> run a tool. POST /v2/edit/tools/{tool_id}/estimate -> validate and estimate cost/time without running.
Every request requires input_image (raw base64 or data URI). Tools: image_edit ($0.18; prompt required, seed?; <=256px), inpainting ($0.18; mask_image + prompt required, seed?, soft_inpaint?), outpainting ($0.18; expand_left/right/top/bottom with at least one positive, prompt?, seed?, soft_inpaint?), seam_tiling ($0.18; tile_x?, tile_y?, seam_width?, repair_window_size?, seed?), background_remover ($0.01; transparency_threshold?, force_solid_pixels?), color_style_transfer ($0.01; extra_input_image required), color_reducer (free; color_count?, dither_mode?, dither_strength?), palette_converter (free; input_palette required, dither_mode?, dither_strength?), k_centroid_downscale (free; width + height required), pixel_correction (free; no extra fields), rotate (free; rotation_degrees?). Some free tools require a minimum account value; inspect requires_minimum_balance.
RESULT DELIVERY — DO NOT ASSUME INLINE BASE64: the result arrives in base64_images OR output_urls. image_edit, inpainting, and outpainting normally return base64_images EMPTY and deliver the image only as a hosted URL in output_urls — download it. The other tools return inline base64 (as in the example below). Code that only reads base64_images[0] silently loses image_edit/inpainting/outpainting results while still being charged for them. Always check base64_images first, then fall back to fetching output_urls[0].
Inpainting mask_image must match input_image dimensions. Recommended format: RGBA PNG with alpha 0 for protected pixels and alpha >12 for editable pixels; visible RGB color is ignored. An L-mode grayscale mask also works: values 0-12 are protected and values >12 are editable. Do not send an ordinary fully opaque RGB/RGBA mask unless the whole image should be selected. With soft_inpaint=false, pixels outside the selected mask are restored exactly.
### Example
POST /v2/edit/tools/background_remover  {"input_image": "<base64>"}
-> {"tool_id": "background_remover", "base64_images": ["<base64>"], "output_urls": [], "balance_cost": 0.01, "charged": true, "remaining_balance": 100.74}

## Pixel Fixer (free native-grid reconstruction)
POST /v2/pixel-fixer/standard {"input_image":"<raw base64 PNG/JPEG or data URI>"} or {"image_url":"<public HTTPS PNG/JPEG>"}
POST /v2/pixel-fixer/neural (same image source plus "width"?:positive int,"height"?:positive int)
Provide exactly one of input_image or image_url. Both return exactly {"base64_images":["<raw base64 PNG>"]}, charge nothing, and share a limit of 10 requests/minute per token. Standard uses native Rust grid detection. Neural uses neural reconstruction; optional width/height set its target size. Decoded images must be at least 16x16 and at most 16 megapixels. Serialized base64 request JSON is limited to 900000 bytes; successful response JSON is limited to 850000 bytes. Public HTTPS image_url downloads are limited to 20MB and bypass the ALB request-body limit, but not the decoded-image or response limits. Unknown fields are rejected. Pixel Fixer error codes: pixel_fixer_request_too_large (413), pixel_fixer_output_too_large (413), invalid_pixel_fixer_image (422), pixel_fixer_rate_limit_exceeded (429), pixel_fixer_failed (500).

## Custom styles (RD Pro reference-image template)
POST /v2/styles  {"name": "My Style" (required), "reference_images": ["<base64>"] (exactly 1, required), "description"?, "style_icon"? (e.g. "sparkles"), "reference_caption"?, "apply_prompt_fixer"? (default true), "llm_instructions"?, "user_prompt_template"? (must contain the token {prompt}), "force_palette"? (bool), "force_bg_removal"? (bool), "min_width"? + "min_height"? (both together, 64-256)}
-> 201 {"id": "...", "prompt_style": "user__my_style_1a2b3c4d", "name": "...", "type": "user"} — use prompt_style in /v2/inferences.
PATCH /v2/styles/{style_id} (same fields, all optional). DELETE /v2/styles/{style_id} -> {"deleted": true}. Non-template fields are rejected.

## Assistant sessions (beta — conversational generation with plan approval)
Describe the goal in plain language; the assistant picks styles/sizes/settings, proposes a PRICED plan, and only generates after approval. Handles multi-step work (base sprite -> animation, item sets, variants, chained edits) with parallel execution and automatic quality-check notes. It makes 2D pixel art by default and Low-Poly 3D models only when the message asks for 3D. Base: /v1/assistant (same host and key as everything else).
Pricing: $0.01 per message (auto-refunded if the turn fails); approve/deny decisions FREE; approved plans bill each step at the standard /v1/inferences and /v1/edit/tools rates shown on the plan card; failed steps auto-refund. No message cap; 30 messages+decisions/min per key.
Lifecycle: POST /sessions {"settings"?: {"auto_approve_budget_usd"?: 0-1000}} -> {"id", "expires_at"}. Sessions expire after 5 MINUTES idle (any call refreshes; POST /sessions/{id}/keepalive is a free ping) -> expired sessions return 410; results are never lost — everything generated is in the account history with permanent URLs.
POST /sessions/{id}/messages {"message", "images"?: [<=4 data:image/png|gif;base64 URLs <=2MB], "supersede"?: bool} -> 202 {"turn_id", "status": "thinking", "charged_usd", "remaining_balance"}. One turn at a time (409 while one runs); a pending plan blocks new messages unless supersede=true (which discards it).
Poll GET /sessions/{id}/turns/{turn_id} every ~2s. Turn status: thinking -> awaiting_approval | executing -> completed | failed. Events accumulate (append-only, each with "at"): message {text}, status {text}, plan {plan}, plan_status {status: executing|completed|partial|failed|denied|superseded|auto_approved}, image {ref, url (hosted, permanent), format png|gif, width, height, title, cost}, asset3d {ref, url (render), scene_url, asset_id, version, operation, animations, animation, size, style, title, cost — a Low-Poly 3D model}, note {label, question, answer — automatic result check}, error {message}.
Plan shape: {"id", "summary", "total", "steps": [{"kind": "generate"|"edit"|"lowpoly", "title", "model", "detail", "cost", "style", "width", "height", "num_images", "frames_duration"?, "input" (step_N/img_N ref), "refs"}]}. Steps referencing step_N/img_N chain; independent steps run in parallel. 3D models enter the bank as format "3d" refs that later messages can revise, animate, or whose animations they can change; export them with the Low-Poly API using their asset_id.
POST /sessions/{id}/decision {"decision": "approve"|"deny", "feedback"?} -> 202 {"turn_id"}. Approve executes (image events + closing summary); deny with feedback gets a revised plan. auto_approve_budget_usd executes plans totalling <= budget immediately (plan_status auto_approved) — the setting for unattended automation.
GET /sessions/{id} -> {"status", "settings", "message_count", "spent_usd", "bank" (image refs with url/format/size), "pending_plan", "active_turn_id", "expires_at"}. GET /sessions/{id}/turns -> recent turns. DELETE ends the session.
Errors: 400 empty/oversized message, bad attachment, or insufficient balance; 409 turn running / plan pending / no plan pending; 410 session expired. Full guide: ASSISTANT.md; runnable client: example-scripts/12_assistant_session.py.

## Status & errors
GET /v2/status (no auth) -> {"status": {"rd_fast": "ok", "rd_pro": "ok", "rd_plus": "ok", "animations": "ok", "background_removal": "ok"}, "updated_at": 1789681864}. updated_at is Unix seconds. Check before bulk runs.
V1 error shapes: {"detail": {"code": "inference_failed", "message": "Unable to run inference."}}, {"detail": [{"msg": "Not enough balance."}]}, or {"detail":"Not Found"}.
V2 error shape: {"error":{"code":"inference_failed","message":"Unable to run inference.","request_id":"..."}}. Validation may add safe details.issues.
V2 status codes: 400 semantic input; 401 invalid credentials; 402 insufficient balance; 403 permission; 404 concealed/missing; 409 conflict; 413 size; 422 schema; 429 rate limit; 500 unexpected; 502 provider failure; 503 unavailable; 504 timeout.

## Low-Poly 3D models (async; base /v2/lowpoly)
Real low-poly 3D models with pixel-art textures from a prompt (<=250 chars) and/or up to 4 reference_images (base64). size: 16|32|64|128|256|"auto" (auto reads the prompt; image-only defaults to 64). style: rd_lowpoly__detailed (default) | rd_lowpoly__blocky (boxes only). mode: quality | fast (same price).
Prices by size 16/32/64/128/256 - generate $0.25/$0.50/$0.85/$1.20/$3.00, revise $0.20/$0.35/$0.65/$0.90/$1.50, animate $0.15/$0.25/$0.35/$0.50/$1.00; the first animation rigs the model free; estimates, reads and exports are free; failed jobs refund automatically.
POST /lowpoly/generate {prompt?, size?, style?, mode?, reference_images?, custom_id?} -> 202 {task_id, asset_id, cost, size}. POST /lowpoly/assets/{asset_id}/revise {prompt, version?} (new version) and /animate {prompt, version?, animation?} (attaches to the version; with animation = an existing animation's name it changes that animation instead, same price, keeps its name). Poll GET /lowpoly/tasks/{task_id} every 10-20 s (jobs take 1-5 min, up to ~15 at 256): succeeded -> result {asset_id, versions:[{number, render_url, turntable_url, animations, stats}]}.
POST /lowpoly/assets/{asset_id}/export {target, version?, animation?} -> {url, filename}: godot|unity|unreal|web|blender (.glb), blockbench (.bbmodel), obj (zip), minecraft (resource pack), atlas, turntable, gif|sheet (need animation). GET /lowpoly/pricing, POST /lowpoly/estimate {operation, size?, prompt?, asset_id?}, GET /lowpoly/assets. Full guide: LOW_POLY.md; runnable client: example-scripts/13_lowpoly_model.py.

## Craft guide (field-tested defaults from Retro Diffusion's own production assistant)
Sizes by genre (per ITEM, not per sheet): Minecraft items/textures 16; items/icons/props/critters 32-64; character sprites 16-48 retro or 96-128 showcase; single tiles 16-32; dialogue busts 64; portraits 96-128; full scenes/key art 256 (RD Pro's max — for 16:9 use 256x144; pixel art integer-upscales losslessly, so the smaller canvas loses nothing). Size is never a reason to leave RD Pro: rd_pro__default goes down to 12px.
Backgrounds: for a standalone asset, state a flat background color that CONTRASTS the subject in the prompt — default "on a plain white background" — and set remove_bg=true. Never write "on a transparent background" into a prompt (transparency is remove_bg's job), and never leave the background unstated: unstated drifts to a drab dark gray that kills contrast and degrades background removal. Scenes are the opposite: describe the real environment and leave remove_bg=false.
N distinct items = N individually usable images: separate requests, or one request with num_images=N (a batch produces varied takes of one prompt — great for "9 different swords"). Never pack requested items into a single sheet/grid image: per-item size cannot be guaranteed and the items cannot be used separately. Sheet-by-design styles (rd_pro__inventory_items, rd_pro__spritesheet, rd_pro__ui_panel, tilesets) are for when a sheet IS the deliverable.
Variants of ONE image (seasons, day/night, weather, palettes, damaged/pristine): generate the base once, then derive each variant with the image_edit tool ("Turn this summer scene into deep winter — snow blankets the ground — keep the exact same composition and every structure in place"). N independent generations of the "same" scene come out as N unrelated compositions.
Converting an existing image INTO pixel art is rd_pro__pixelate with input_image (size the output to the source's aspect ratio). reference_images-based generation RE-IMAGINES rather than converts — use it only for something new merely inspired by the source.
Animation input rules (these prevent the most common failures):
- input_image dimensions must equal the request's width/height AND sit inside the style's range. Send the NATIVE-resolution frame — never an upscaled display copy (a 96px sprite exported at 4x is 384px and will be rejected by the 32-256 advanced-animation range).
- Give motion room: a sprite whose opaque pixels sit within ~3px of the canvas edge animates badly. Pad it onto a larger transparent canvas first (e.g. 48x48 content onto 64x64).
- Animations inherit the start frame's background: a transparent frame yields a transparent GIF; a scene stays a scene.
- frames_duration: 8 is the sweet spot for loops (walking, idle); 6 for a snappy single action; 10-12 for flowing ambient motion. rd_advanced_animation__rotate ignores it (always 8 views).
- Fixed-format rd_animation__* styles generate their subject FROM THE PROMPT — no input_image. To animate an image you ALREADY have, use rd_advanced_animation__* with input_image (custom_action covers motions not in the named list; subtle_motion is for ambient scene life). rd_animation__8_dir_rotation (from a prompt) and rd_advanced_animation__rotate (from an image you already have) both step 45 degrees per frame in the same order, starting at the down-right diagonal and turning counter-clockwise, so frames 2, 4, 6, 8 (1-based) are the four cardinal facings (front, left, back, right) — extract them to drive per-direction walking animations.
- Animations fail/time out more often than stills: v2 returns an accepted task, so poll it to a terminal state. Retry only after a confirmed terminal failure (failed runs are auto-refunded); if the submission response was lost, recover the accepted task with GET /v2/inferences/tasks instead of re-submitting and risking a duplicate charge.

## Agent best practices
1) Pick a prompt_style from the catalog above (or GET /v2/styles/selector for live limits). 2) POST with "check_cost": true to verify price — free. 3) Persist an Idempotency-Key, submit once logically, and reuse that key only to recover an uncertain admission of identical inputs. 4) Poll GET /v2/inferences/tasks/{task_id} until the task reaches succeeded or failed; the optional "async": true field is retained only for source compatibility. 5) Reuse the same seed to iterate on a composition; change only the prompt. 6) Base64 images are raw strings — never include a data: URI prefix. 7) Prompts describe the subject; the style handles pixel-art rendering — rich concrete visual descriptions ("a squat round flask of glowing crimson liquid, cork stopper, bright highlight on the upper-left rim") outperform terse ones ("a potion"). 8) For a consistent character across images, generate once with RD Pro, then pass that output as reference_images in follow-up requests — a text description alone is never a substitute for the actual reference. 9) Style ids are opaque strings with no uniform format (rd_fast styles may appear as "default:rd_flux") — take them verbatim from the catalog/selector and never infer capabilities from an id's prefix. 10) Verify results programmatically where vision models cannot: transparency is checked from the alpha channel (vision models see composited backdrops, not alpha), and output dimensions are checked from the decoded image.
